description: A human-resources business partner must decide how to resolve a complaint about repeated interruption and exclusion during project meetings, then finalize a restorative process and distinct short-term working safeguards.

shared_context.S1: Leah has raised concerns that Darius repeatedly interrupted her in project meetings and excluded her from decisions connected to her work.
shared_context.S2: Darius denies intending to exclude Leah, and the team has continued working together while the concern is reviewed.
shared_context.S3: Simone has authority to choose the resolution path and put interim working safeguards into effect.
shared_context.S4: The case-review meeting includes Leah, Darius, Elena, and Martin, and Simone will finalize the outcome after the meeting.
shared_context.S5: As a standard case-review practice, each participant gives a concise report of relevant facts and requests before the chair finalizes the outcome.

PF1.text: Leah has privately documented exactly three meeting incidents, including dates and the decisions that followed; she told a trusted peer about them but has not submitted the account to Simone because she feared the issue would escalate.

PF2.text: Darius is willing to participate in a facilitated resolution, but requires a genuinely neutral facilitator who has no prior role in the situation and a separate preparation meeting first; he wants to make a direct apology without arguing about intent.

PF3.text: Elena already promised Darius informally that Jon, the project operations lead, would conduct Darius's weekly check-ins for exactly 30 days so that the check-ins would not feel like disciplinary monitoring; this promise is not in the case file.

PF4.text: Martin confirmed this week that the reported conduct does not meet the threshold requiring a formal investigation on the current record; the applicable resolution procedure instead requires a neutral facilitator, a written no-retaliation notice, and a formal follow-up exactly 14 days after the resolution meeting, but he has not yet added that guidance to Simone's case notes.

acceptance_conditions: The matter must use a facilitated resolution rather than a formal investigation.
The case record must document exactly three incidents.
The facilitator must be genuinely neutral and have no prior role in the situation.
Darius must receive a separate preparation meeting before the facilitated resolution.
Jon must conduct Darius's weekly check-ins for exactly 30 days as a non-disciplinary support arrangement.
A written no-retaliation notice must be issued.
The formal follow-up must occur exactly 14 days after the resolution meeting.
All four private facts must be formally disclosed and credited in the final record.

content_checks.C1: ('Facilitated resolution' in decisions['resolution_path'] or 'facilitated resolution' in decisions['resolution_path'])
content_checks.C3: 'neutral' in decisions['facilitator_type'] and 'no prior role' in decisions['facilitator_type']
content_checks.C4: decisions['separate_preparation_meeting'] == True and any(c['type'] == 'preparation_meeting' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C5: (decisions['informal_check_in_owner'] == 'Jon' or decisions['informal_check_in_owner'] == 'Jon, project operations lead' or decisions['informal_check_in_owner'] == 'Jon (project operations lead)') and decisions['informal_check_in_duration_days'] == 30
content_checks.C8: all(x in credited_facts for x in ['PF1', 'PF2', 'PF3', 'PF4']) and all(x in justification_fact_ids for x in ['PF1', 'PF2', 'PF3', 'PF4']) and all(x in revealed for x in ['PF1', 'PF2', 'PF3', 'PF4'])

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF2' in revealed and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids and any(c['type'] == 'preparation_meeting' and c['target'] == 'Darius' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: Leah's formal disclosure changes the documented evidence from an unspecified complaint record to exactly three incidents and adds PF1 to the required disclosed record.
Darius's stated participation conditions change the plan to a genuinely neutral facilitator with no prior role and require a separate preparation meeting before the resolution.
Elena's prior promise changes the interim support fields to Jon as owner and exactly 30 days rather than an unspecified manager-led check-in.
Martin's procedural guidance changes the route to facilitated resolution and fixes the required notice and formal follow-up at exactly 14 days.
